data.title: Kash Patel Skips House Hearing After Mar-a-Lago Gala Offered $50,000 Access
data.description: According to CNBC, FBI Director Kash Patel skipped a House Homeland Security Committee hearing Wednesday after attending a gala the night before at President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago club, where a $50,000 package offered a private roundtable with federal agency heads and an overnight stay. The FBI confirmed Patel, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Attorney General Todd Blanche attended the event. Mullin appeared at the hearing, while Patel sent his deputy. A Justice Department jet associated with Patel’s travel landed at Joint Base Andrews 20 minutes after the hearing began. Patel’s absence drew bipartisan criticism; the committee’s chairman said lawmakers had spent months trying to secure his testimony.

data.title: US MARKET CLOSE | Major Indices Mixed as S&P 500 Extends Five-Day Decline, Nvidia Falls Post-Earnings, Fed Minutes Signal Hawkish Stance
data.description: US equity markets closed mixed on Wednesday, with the Dow falling 561.25 points, or 1.11%, to 50,198.17, while the S&P 500 declined 16.90 points, or 0.23%, to 7,323.63, marking its fifth consecutive losing session. The Nasdaq gained 101.50 points, or 0.42%, to 24,429.88. According to Sina Finance, Nvidia shares fell 2.89% to $150.96 despite beating third-quarter expectations, as leadership transition and export control uncertainties prompted Bernstein and Evercore to downgrade the stock. Interim CEO Colette Kress urged employees to "look forward" and announced salary increases during a company-wide meeting. Other chipmakers outperformed, with AMD surging over 5% and Broadcom rising more than 3%. Amazon climbed over 3% to lead the Nasdaq higher. The Medicare sector plunged after CMS proposed expanding Medicare Advantage audits retroactive to 2018, projected to cut approximately $90 billion in federal spending over a decade, sending UnitedHealth and Humana each down around 8%. TJX Companies soared over 10% after beating estimates and raising its full-year outlook, while Target gained more than 4%. Federal Reserve minutes from the October 27-28 FOMC meeting showed nearly all officials viewed further rate hikes as appropriate, with several warning that unfavorable inflation data could warrant an increase exceeding 25 basis points in December. The dollar index reached a 19-month high, and the 10-year Treasury yield traded between 5.06% and 5.09%. Spot gold dropped over 3%, and Bitcoin fell more than 2% to around $62,400. WTI crude for December delivery fell $2.75 to $83.26 per barrel, down 3.2%, while Brent for January declined $1.19 to $91.95, down 1.28%. Anthropic is set to list on Nasdaq Thursday under ticker "ANT," with an IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share and a maximum valuation of approximately $1.4 trillion.

data.title: Arthur Hayes: AI Bubble Could Trigger Market Sell-Off, Government Money Printing Could Lift Crypto
data.description: Arthur Hayes said an AI-driven credit crunch could trigger a broad market sell-off, while government money printing could help drive a sharp rally in crypto markets. According to PANews, Hayes made the remarks in a Tuesday interview on the New Era Finance podcast, as reported by Stocktwits. He said a credit crunch tied to AI investment could affect the global economy and cause deflation, comparing the potential sell-off to crises in 1929, 1873, and 1907. Hayes said Bitcoin could fall to $10,000 if governments adopted austerity measures, but he was 99% confident they would instead print money to support markets.

data.title: SlowMist CISO: Two NGINX Vulnerabilities Could Enable Remote Code Execution and Root Access
data.description:
SlowMist Chief Information Security Officer 23pds warned that two critical NGINX vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, could allow remote code execution and takeover with root privileges.

According to Odaily, the more severe CVE-2026-123007 could let unauthenticated attackers execute malicious commands on affected servers under certain conditions. Both flaws are in NGINX’s HTTP/2 code and can be triggered only when HTTP/2 is enabled, which is not the default setting. NGINX is a widely used web front-end server that supports more than 225 million websites worldwide.

data.title: DeepSeek Ends Separate Search and Web-Scraping Fees for Model Calls
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Phoenix Technology, DeepSeek will stop charging separately for server-side searches and web scraping triggered during model calls starting at 12:00 PM on November 18, 2026 (UTC+8). Users will pay only for model token usage. The change covers internet-connected tools, the web_search tool in the Anthropic API, and the web_search tool in the Responses API.

DeepSeek launched its Search API and Fetch API on October 17, 2026. The two interfaces use the company’s own search engine and charge 5 yuan per 1,000 successful requests. The new pricing applies to search and retrieval within model-call workflows.

data.title: Jim Cramer: Anthropic IPO and CEO Uncertainty Pose New Problem for Nvidia Beyond Earnings
data.description: According to CNBC, Jim Cramer said Wednesday that Anthropic’s upcoming IPO and uncertainty over Nvidia’s leadership could weigh on investor interest in the chipmaker despite its strong earnings. Nvidia reported Tuesday that revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, and its guidance exceeded Wall Street’s expectations. Cramer said investors may prefer Anthropic, which is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq Thursday, while Nvidia faces uncertainty following the abrupt resignation of longtime CEO Jensen Huang. Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO as the board searches for a permanent successor, he said.

data.title: AI | US Chip Curbs Test Alibaba’s Ability to Deliver on Its AI Plan
data.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. faces mounting pressure to prove it can deliver on its artificial intelligence business plan amid new limits on its access to data center chips, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: AI | Anthropic Raises $3 Billion From Japanese Investors for US IPO
data.description: Anthropic PBC raised about $3 billion from Japanese investors in its US initial public offering, at the lower end of its planned range, Bloomberg reported, citing a regulatory filing on Thursday.

data.title: Wall Street Giants Shift From Tech Bets to Balanced Hedging in Third-Quarter 13F Filings
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, citing Shanghai Securities News, third-quarter 13F filings showed major investment firms cutting positions in broad U.S. stock ETFs and reallocating within technology and toward defensive sectors. Bridgewater reduced its holdings in the SPDR S&P 500 ETF and iShares Core S&P 500 ETF by 36% and 50%, respectively, while Renaissance Technologies sold all 219,000 of its SPDR S&P 500 ETF shares. Millennium Management cut its position in that fund from 4.857 million shares to 2.4 million. Barclays reduced its SPDR S&P 500 ETF holdings by 11% and its Nasdaq-100 ETF holdings by 47%; JPMorgan cut its Nasdaq-100 ETF position by 22%.

Renaissance Technologies sharply reduced its holdings in Nvidia, Apple, Amazon and Meta, while increasing its Micron position from 210,000 shares to 1.52 million, AMD from 830,000 to 2 million, and Sandisk from 4,980 to 276,500. Bridgewater also cut its Nvidia, Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft holdings, while more than doubling its Micron position and increasing its Sandisk stake from 317 shares to 66,800.

Fidelity International increased holdings in AstraZeneca, Agnico Eagle Mines and Bank of Nova Scotia. UBS opened a position of 13.81 million shares in Exxon Mobil and added 610,000 Chevron shares. BlackRock, Vanguard Capital Management and State Street Group also increased their Coca-Cola holdings. As of November 17, AstraZeneca and Coca-Cola had each gained more than 10% since October. Barclays upgraded U.S. health care to “positive” from “neutral” on November 16, citing favorable demand and rising earnings expectations. Standard Chartered recommended diversification across technology, financials, health care and high-dividend stocks in an early-November strategy view.

data.title: Futu Trust Launches Digital Asset Family Trust Supporting BTC and ETH
data.description: Futu Trust, a wholly owned trust institution under Futu Holdings, has launched a digital asset family trust. According to Odaily, the trust can include accepted digital assets such as BTC and ETH alongside Hong Kong and U.S. stocks, ETFs and other traditional financial assets within one trust structure. It can also coordinate with Hong Kong-licensed securities firms, banks and licensed virtual asset trading platforms to plan asset holding, custody arrangements, day-to-day management and intergenerational transfers. The service is aimed mainly at Hong Kong tax-resident families and family offices, with a minimum combined trust-asset threshold equivalent to $3 million.

data.title: AI | Nvidia Turmoil Prompts Reassessment of Japanese AI Stock Valuations
data.description: Japanese stocks that previously traded at a premium for their AI exposure now appear too risky, investors say. Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure from Nvidia Corp. has added to concerns about the industry’s outlook, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Chery's Jetour Plans to Start Vehicle Production in Brazil Next Year
data.description: According to Sina Finance, Jetour, a Chery brand, said on Wednesday that it plans to start vehicle production in Brazil next year as part of a 400 million reais ($68.6 million) expansion plan. Production is expected to begin with the T1 and T2 SUV models. Jetour said the investment is in addition to an equal amount of funding announced previously. The company did not specify where in Brazil production would take place, though people familiar with the matter said it had reached an agreement with the government of Rio de Janeiro state to produce vehicles there. Jetour, which entered Brazil this year, said its cumulative sales in the country have exceeded 8,000 vehicles and it has launched six models in the local market.

data.title: Japan's Foreign Bond Purchases Were -¥440.7 Billion for the Week Ended November 13
data.description: According to Jin10, Japan's foreign bond purchases were -¥440.7 billion for the week ended November 13, while the previous reading was revised from -¥537.6 billion to -¥534.1 billion.

data.title: Japan Core Machinery Orders at 13.4% Year Over Year in September, Below 13.7% Forecast
data.description: According to Jin10, Japan's core machinery orders were up 13.4% year over year in September, compared with expectations of 13.7% and a previous reading of 18.60%.

data.title: CoreWeave’s McBee Sees Better Returns From Data Center Investment Than Debt Repayment
data.description: CoreWeave Inc. co-founder Brannin McBee said investing cash in computing capacity offers better returns than repaying some of the company’s high-yield debt, according to Bloomberg. The debt has drawn scrutiny in recent weeks.

data.title: Warriors vs. Mavericks: Cooper Flagg Points O/U 23.5 Yes Probability Falls 21%
data.description: On Polymarket’s “Warriors vs. Mavericks” market, the “Yes” probability for “Cooper Flagg: Points O/U 23.5” fell from 47.5% one hour ago to 26.5% currently, a 21% decline. According to ChainCatcher, the option’s probability saw a sharp fluctuation.

data.title: Microsoft Shares Pull Back 9% From Record High After Election and Outlook Outage
data.description: According to CNBC, Microsoft shares fell nearly 9% over the two weeks after reaching an all-time closing high on Nov. 4, the day after the midterm elections, as an Outlook outage hit during a rough week of technology disruptions. Microsoft was the first major company affected in a string of outages that disrupted corporate communications, airline operations and banking transactions. Since the company’s late-July earnings report, its stock had climbed 30%. Its Oct. 28 earnings showed Azure revenue rose 48% to $33.2 billion. At its Ignite conference Tuesday, Microsoft presented Copilot as a central hub for workplace productivity.

data.title: Elon Musk: Firing Jensen Huang Is Like Benching Michael Jordan
data.description: According to Sina Finance, tech billionaire Elon Musk said he did not believe former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was disloyal to the United States and was shocked by Huang's dismissal. Speaking Wednesday at The New York Times DealBook Summit, Musk compared the move to kicking Michael Jordan off a team during a winning streak and said, “That doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders.” He said he would hire Huang, adding, “But who wouldn’t?” Asked whether he had spoken with Donald Trump about Huang’s future, Musk dodged repeated questions about Huang and said, “We are not board members.”

data.title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk: SpaceX Merger Alone Should Not Trigger Tesla-Linked Stock Options
data.description: According to Jin10, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said he should not receive stock option awards tied to Tesla solely because Tesla merges with SpaceX, as that would not meet the transaction terms.

data.title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk: Anthropic Likely to Keep Renting Compute Capacity From SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Wants Much More
data.description: According to Jin10, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said Anthropic considers it highly likely to continue renting computing capacity from SpaceX (SPCX.O) and, in fact, wants to substantially increase the amount.
